Defunct R35 Nissan GT-R Drags Retired C8 Chevy Corvette E-Ray, Someone Gets Destroyed in 8.31s
14 photos
Photo: Wheels / YouTube
The R35 Nissan GT-R has been around since December 2007, and nobody was ultimately surprised when it bowed out from production last summer. But the C8 generation of the iconic Chevrolet Corvette is much younger and, surprisingly, it already has defunct versions – well, one, that is.
The Japanese grand tourer – aka Godzilla for enthusiasts – had a long stint, surviving the massive changes across the sports car market for almost 18 years. It had a long, clean, and very good run, and we’re not surprised if some folks already consider it a legend among its peers.
On the other hand, the C8 debuted back in 2019 with the biggest change a Chevrolet Corvette had ever seen – it switched from a classic front-engine RWD format to the mid-engine setup. It also gained, for the first time, all-wheel drive and a performance hybrid powertrain, all courtesy of the newly introduced E-Ray version.
However, it was a short-lived premiere, and for the 2027 model year General Motors introduced a brand-new 6.7-liter V8 engine used for the base Stingray along with the returning Grand Sport and the first-ever Grand Sport X. While the former two have 535 hp and 520 lb-ft of torque both, the third option gained the ZR1X’s electrified setup and together with the new V8 churns out 721 hp, much more than E-Ray’s previous 655 combined horsepower.
Nevertheless, a C8 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray is never an opponent that should be trifled with, since it has AWD and can launch like a rocket thanks to its hybrid setup. Well, the videographer behind the ' Wheels ' channel on YouTube recently took a detour around Bradenton Motorsports Park in Florida for the local FL2K competition, and showed us a feisty America versus Import brawl thanks to the meeting between a crimson R35 Nissan GT-R and a Hysteria Purple E-Ray.
We don’t know if both cars are stock, though it’s pretty obvious that either driver has opted at least for a beefier track tire and wheel setup. Well, as it turns out, the R35 Nissan GT-R simply destroyed the all-wheel-drive and hybrid-assisted E-Ray right off the line – the driver’s reaction time was absolutely bonkers (0.02!).
The car wasn’t any less, either, as it raised its nose and kept it up while accelerating like there’s no tomorrow, leaving the Corvette far behind. In the end, the difference was pretty obvious: 10.49s for the E-Ray at 126 mph while the Godzilla crossed the line at BMP in just 8.31s and at a lower trap speed of 121 mph.
So, what do you think? Are you eagerly awaiting the next-generation Nissan GT-R, which could also be a performance hybrid just like the E-Ray? Maybe we’ll see the R36 in a clash with the more powerful C8 Grand Sport X in the not-so-distant future…
